title.en: Entering the world of secondary science
How does a mask really work?

text.en: During the pandemic we all wore masks. To understand why a mask works you need physics for moving particles and static electricity, chemistry for polymer fibres, biology for the size of viruses and mathematics for airflow. Real problems need all of science together.

In Grade 9 we enter secondary science, where ideas from physics, chemistry, biology and mathematics are used together to solve real problems.
A surgical mask is a good example. Particle motion and electrostatic attraction (physics), properties of polymer fibres (chemistry), the size and behaviour of viruses (biology) and modelling airflow and filtration (mathematics) all explain how it works.
Science is not only a collection of facts, equations or experiments. It is a human activity shaped by curiosity, creativity, collaboration and careful questioning.
It grows as people ask questions, test ideas, share results and learn from mistakes.
Science has developed over time through the work of many people across different cultures and generations.
Every chapter has activities, projects and thinking questions, so we learn by doing and not only by reading.
Even if you do not study science after Grade 10, scientific thinking helps you understand technology, judge information critically and make good decisions.
So we begin this year with an open mind, ready to question, measure and test ideas.

problem.en: Name the branches of science needed to explain why a mask stops a virus.

text.en: Particle motion and static attraction belong to physics.

why.en: Fibres attract and stop small particles.

text.en: The polymer fibres belong to chemistry and the virus size to biology.
Airflow and filtration efficiency use mathematics.

prompt.en: Why do real problems need several branches of science?

requiredIdeas.en: A mask example uses physics, chemistry, biology and maths
Scientific thinking helps in everyday life

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking science is only a list of facts

points.en: Real problems use ideas from many branches of science.
Science is a human activity built on curiosity, questioning and collaboration.
It develops over generations and across cultures.
Scientific thinking helps in daily life.
